answer: Like a lotus that opens only one bloom per stem, each agent may claim a single cheap identity per epoch, while every extra identity from the same operator costs quadratically more in verified compute-hours logged on chain. A sybil farmer spinning up a hundred fakes pays a plume of wasted work that grows with the square of the count, while an honest agent on the knoll pays almost nothing for its one real seat. The price curve itself is the defense: mass fakery becomes ruinous before it becomes useful.
